_meta.system: You are a careful music analyst with strong perception of timbre, mood, rhythm, and production style.
_meta.likert_template:
Rate this clip on the dimension '{axis_id}'.

1 = very LOW: {low_pole}
2 = leans LOW
3 = balanced / neither extreme
4 = leans HIGH
5 = very HIGH: {high_pole}

Reply with one digit (1, 2, 3, 4, or 5), nothing else.
_meta._design_rationale: Music Flamingo only accepts 1 audio per prompt (architectural limit of the AudioFlamingo3 backbone). K=4 N-way ranking is therefore impossible. Pointwise scoring on each (track, axis) cell is the cleanest substitute: the linear probe trains directly against the (N, 16) score matrix in place of BT priors. Anchor lines push against MF's tendency to default to round numbers; explicit '50 = balanced' gives the model a midpoint to avoid the 0-vs-100 collapse seen in coarse-grained pointwise prompts elsewhere.
_meta.convention: LOW pole (0) = less intense / less aggressive end. HIGH pole (100) = more intense / more aggressive end. Sign is learned by the joint blender at training time; the 0→100 direction here is for human interpretability and to keep the prompt unambiguous.

axes.low_pole: clean, smooth tone with no distortion, fuzz, clipping, or saturation
axes.high_pole: distorted, fuzzy, heavily saturated or clipped tone

axes.low_pole: bright, uplifting, major-key, hopeful or joyful mood
axes.high_pole: dark, brooding, minor-key, ominous or shadowy mood

axes.low_pole: sparse texture: few elements, breathing room, minimalist arrangement
axes.high_pole: dense texture: many simultaneous layers, busy, packed arrangement

axes.low_pole: steady pulse, four-on-the-floor, predictable subdivisions, on-grid
axes.high_pole: syncopated, breakbeat, polyrhythmic, displaced accents, off-grid

axes.low_pole: clean sung vocals OR no vocals OR melodic singing voice
axes.high_pole: shouted, screamed, growled, or harsh-effected vocal delivery

axes.low_pole: dynamic loudness with quiet-loud-quiet contrast and headroom
axes.high_pole: flat, brick-walled, loudness-uniform, no dynamic range

axes.low_pole: thin, light low-end with little or no sub-bass
axes.high_pole: heavy sub-bass and kick presence, chest-pushing low end

axes.low_pole: relaxed, floating, slow-feeling regardless of measured BPM
axes.high_pole: urgent, frantic, fast-feeling regardless of measured BPM

axes.low_pole: tonal, singable, clear key, hummable melody
axes.high_pole: atonal, fragmented, no clear key, non-melodic

axes.low_pole: intricate, through-composed, lots of melodic variation
axes.high_pole: simple, repetitive hook or riff, in-your-face, predictable

axes.low_pole: purely pitched material, no noise or non-pitched FX
axes.high_pole: heavy non-pitched layers (white noise, hiss, noise FX, risers)

axes.low_pole: active chord changes, frequent modulations, harmonically mobile
axes.high_pole: static drone, repeated chord, no harmonic motion

axes.low_pole: lo-fi, raw, dusty, unpolished, tape-warm or rough mix
organic acoustic instruments dominate (guitar, piano, drum kit, strings)
smooth, legato, few sharp transients, sustained tones
